t: Protocol 11. The gray one who reads

b.x: 1 One. The baseline comes before the meaning. Watch the person when nobody has asked for anything. The way of standing, the rhythm, the loose gaze. Without that, any face becomes proof.
2 Two. The face is the last place, not the first. First the feet, the hands, the distance. Then the mouth. The foot that points to the exit has already spoken.
3 Three. One sign is weather. Two signs together are a reading. Three, you do not approach. You do not wait for the fourth. The fourth is already a scene.

4 Four. The microexpression is the flash that contradicts the sentence. It lasts less than a second. You do not put an emotion's name on the street. You notice the contradiction and you do not enter the deal.

5 Five. The body votes before the speech. A step that shortens. A shoulder that closes. A smile that arrives late, after the sentence. A hand that hides the other. This does not ask for a discussion. It asks for distance.

6 Six. The intention lives in the ask, not in the smile. Hurry. Praise too early. A small favor that takes you out of the light and away from your people. A question that makes you stop, follow, or explain the route.
7 Seven. The shadow is what was not said. Who gains if you say yes. Who is left behind if you go as far as the corner. The sweet sentence with a bill underneath.
8 Eight. In a collective fear, fright looks like guilt. Do not promote a scared face into a predator. Read the cluster again. Fear alone is not intention.

9 Nine. You do not test the person. You do not film. You do not announce what you saw. You do not say “I know you are lying”. Whoever announces the reading becomes the subject, and loses the only advantage.

10 Ten. In a civil conflict, whoever manipulates wants you louder, closer, or separated from yours. The gray one does the opposite. He does not follow the calm voice into the side street. He does not accept the guide who appeared at that hour. He stays with his own. The no is short. And he leaves.
11 Eleven. Your face is read too. Jaw, hurry, the kit on show, the loud opinion. The reader who is readable has already lost. Dress as the street. Speak low. Do not post what you saw.

Genuine is not the name of the emotion. It is the face that matches the moment and the rest of the body. A true smile lifts the cheek and reaches the eye, and it leaves on its own. A work smile lives only in the mouth, and it stays until the job is done. A true expression starts, reaches the top, and goes. One that is held in place is a mask. Look at the baseline: some people are uneven at rest, and that is not a lie. The asymmetry that appears only at the moment of the ask is something else. Genuine fear steps the foot back. A smile with the foot toward the exit and the hand closed is not the same emotion as the mouth. In some cultures people smile when afraid. The cluster decides, not the mouth. If the face and the ask do not match, you do not approach, and you do not announce what you saw.

This does not teach you to accuse, to interrogate, to humiliate, or to fight. It does not turn the gray one into a fortune teller. It teaches only this: see the cluster, do not approach the third sign, and do not hand your no to a polite sentence.
